sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Zahir Hossain Baidya's poetry is rooted in the intensity of feeling and the effort to give it a written form. His contribution to Fakir Chand College's 2022–23 magazine, The Lone-Wolf, identifies him as an English Honours student. That dated publication provides an early point of reference for the questioning, emotionally charged voice encountered in his work here.

Sinister Sense begins with a reported proposal about stray dogs, then turns its attention to the human threat faced by women in public places. Its harsh, deliberately disturbing questions give way to an appeal for protection. The poem's animal and floral imagery makes a pointed contrast between predation and vulnerable life; the speaker's anger is part of its rhetoric, rather than a biographical account of the poet.
